explanation: Degrees and radians are two ways to name the same angle. The 'angle' slider sets how far the radius arm sweeps; the orange arc shows the angle opening up. Radians measure that angle by the arc it cuts on a circle of radius 1, which is why a full turn is 2π (about 6.28) instead of 360. The readout shows the same angle written both ways, plus what fraction of a full turn it is.
bullets: Multiply degrees by π/180 to get radians; multiply radians by 180/π to go back.
180° = π rad, 360° = 2π rad: a half turn is π, a full turn is 2π.
Radians are the angle's arc length on a unit circle — a pure ratio, no units.
